title: Third-Party Buyouts: What to Ask Before You Assume Anything
description: Whether an outside financing company can complete your lease buyout depends on your leasing company and sometimes your state. Here is how to find out without guessing.
body:
A common lease-end assumption is that you can walk into any bank, credit union, or financing company and use them to buy your leased car. Sometimes that is true. Sometimes it is not. The honest answer is that it depends, and it depends on rules you can look up.

Two different questions

People often mix these up:

  1. Can you buy the car? Almost every lessee has a purchase option in the contract.
  2. Can someone else fund that purchase? This is a policy question for the leasing company, and it can vary by brand, by program, and over time.

Because policies change, we do not list any single company's rule on this site. What stays true is the method for finding out.

Where the answer lives

  • Your contract: look for the purchase option clause and any language about assignment or third parties.
  • Your lease-end letter: some include instructions for outside financing, some say nothing.
  • The buyout department: ask directly. Note the name and date.
  • Your financing partner: a company that regularly closes lease buyouts will know what each leasing company requires in practice.

What a financing partner typically needs

Requirements vary, but you will usually be asked for your account information, a current payoff quote, the vehicle identification number, the odometer reading, and your own financial documents. The leasing company will have its own process for receiving payment and releasing the title to a new lienholder.

Possible snags, and what they mean

  • "We only sell to the lessee." Ask whether the lessee can buy first and have financing in place at closing. Different structures may be allowed.
  • A dealer-only requirement. Some leasing companies route sales through a franchised dealer. That can add a step and a fee. Ask what it is.
  • Different rules for different states. Where you live, and where the car is titled, may change the process.

A note on how we talk about this

Champion Auto Finance is a financing partner, not a lender, and approvals and terms depend on lender underwriting. That is why we encourage you to confirm the leasing company's requirements first. It saves time for everyone, and it avoids paying for a plan that cannot close.

Next step

If you have your payoff quote, a good follow-up is to check your numbers against the market using this guide. If you want to talk it through, you can ask Joe a question.
